# Add a `--quiet` flag to `faff runcheck`

## WHY
`faff runcheck` prints a per-issue audit line plus a summary. In a CI step the per-issue lines are noise; only the final pass/fail and exit code matter.

## WHAT
`faff runcheck --quiet` suppresses the per-issue lines and prints only the one-line summary; the exit code is unchanged (0 clean, non-zero on a dangling admitted issue).

## HOW
**Chosen:** thread a `quiet` boolean from the arg parser into the existing report loop and gate each per-issue `console.log` on `!quiet`. The summary line and exit code paths are untouched, so the machine-consumed contract is identical.

**Punt:** whether to also expose a `--force` escape hatch that re-enables the per-issue lines even under a globally-quiet CI env var, or rely on callers simply dropping `--quiet` — needs a human call, but it does not block the core flag work, which is correct either way.

## DONE
- [ ] `faff runcheck --quiet` prints only the summary line on a clean run
- [ ] the exit code is byte-identical to the non-quiet run on both clean and dangling inputs
- [ ] a unit test asserts the suppressed per-issue lines and the unchanged exit code

The core work is fully specified; one non-blocking open question remains on the escape-hatch shape.
